source.title: Types for tame p-adic groups
readSections: Entire accepted author manuscript v2, §§1–8, all proofs, footnotes and references (39 pages).
Official published abstract and bibliographic metadata; published Annals full text not obtained, so no proof-by-proof published-version comparison is asserted.
Fintzen, On the construction of tame supercuspidal representations, published Compositio 157 (2021), 2733–2746: entire §§1–4 and references.
Kim–Yu, Construction of Tame Types, arXiv:1612.04204v1: §§3.1–3.6, 4.1–4.3, 7.1 tail–7.5 including proof, §10.1–10.3 including proof. §8.1–8.2 encountered but not imported.

source.version: arXiv v2, 3 November 2020; all unqualified page numbers below refer to this 39-page version.

summary: Extracts the tame-prime datum-existence theorem, Kim–Yu type exhaustion, Yu supercuspidal exhaustion and the maximal-datum criterion. The main manuscript and the corrected construction companion are fully read. Status remains partial because foundational source closure and several exact proof adapters require further work; nothing is claimed formalized.
conventions: All representations in the target theorems are smooth complex representations; no modular-coefficient or residue-characteristic-two extension is inferred.
The local field may have positive characteristic. Tameness and p∤|W_abs| remain separate hypotheses. Non-tori have p odd under this bound; the torus case is treated separately.
The additive character φ has conductor the maximal ideal P: trivial on P and nontrivial on o. Field extensions retain the base-k valuation normalization.
Use enlarged buildings, connected parahoric models, and distinguish point stabilizers from reduced-building stabilizers. The latter give the compact-mod-center inducing subgroup.
Depth indices use real r and r+ with r<r+<s<s+ for r<s. Lie/dual depths may be negative; group depths are nonnegative.
Each candidate route is a proposal, not an accepted supplier; every item assigned to a candidate remains missing.

items.name: Nonarchimedean local field
items.statement: For a field k with valuative relation and topology, IsNonarchimedeanLocalField asserts a compatible valuative topology, local compactness and a nontrivial valuation. Residue finiteness and discrete valuation are consequences, not extra characteristic-zero assumptions.

items.name: Normalized base valuation
items.statement: For a nonarchimedean local field k, normalizedValuation k is a homomorphism k×→Multiplicative Z with a uniformizer of additive value 1. Its zero-preserving extension is available; interpreting zero as additive +∞ requires an explicit order-convention adapter.

items.name: Additive character carrier
items.statement: For an additive monoid A and multiplicative monoid M, AddChar A M consists of maps preserving zero-to-one and addition-to-multiplication. The paper specializes to k→C×; continuity and conductor are additional properties.

items.name: Linear representation carrier
items.statement: For a semiring R, monoid H and R-module V, Representation R H V is a monoid homomorphism H→End_R(V). Smoothness, irreducibility and topology are separate conditions in the present application.

items.name: Fixed submodule
items.statement: For a commutative ring R, group H and R-linear representation ρ on V, Representation.invariants ρ is {v | ∀h,ρ(h)v=v}. Subgroup invariants are invariants of the restriction.

items.name: Smooth complex representation
items.statement: Let k be a nonarchimedean local field of residue characteristic p, G a connected reductive k-group split by a tame extension, and p∤|W_abs(G)|. A complex representation of G(k) is smooth when each vector has an open stabilizer; irreducible means nonzero with no proper nonzero stable subspace. Finite-dimensional invariants are a theorem for irreducibles, not part of this definition.

items.name: Complex supercuspidality
items.statement: Let k be a nonarchimedean local field of residue characteristic p, G a connected reductive k-group split by a tame extension, and p∤|W_abs(G)|. An irreducible smooth π is supercuspidal when it is not a subquotient of parabolic induction from any proper k-Levi. Its equivalent Jacquet-module and compact-mod-center matrix-coefficient criteria are supplied by SR.2–3.

items.name: Bernstein inertial class
items.statement: Let k be a nonarchimedean local field of residue characteristic p, G a connected reductive k-group split by a tame extension, and p∤|W_abs(G)|. An inertial class s consists of G(k)-conjugacy classes of pairs (L,σ), L a k-Levi and σ an irreducible supercuspidal L(k)-representation, modulo unramified-character twist. R^s(G) is the corresponding smooth complex block.

items.name: Compact induction and Frobenius reciprocity
items.statement: For a locally profinite group H and open subgroup J, construct c-Ind_J^H τ from locally constant τ-equivariant functions compactly supported modulo J. For smooth complex π there is a natural Hom_H(c-Ind τ,π)≃Hom_J(τ,π|J). A compact-mod-center J need not be compact.

items.name: Bernstein block decomposition
items.statement: Let k be a nonarchimedean local field of residue characteristic p, G a connected reductive k-group split by a tame extension, and p∤|W_abs(G)|. The smooth complex category decomposes as the product of its Bernstein blocks. The type criterion below concerns every irreducible in one block, not merely a single representation containing ρ.

items.name: Bernstein type
items.statement: Let k be a nonarchimedean local field of residue characteristic p, G a connected reductive k-group split by a tame extension, and p∤|W_abs(G)|. For compact open K⊂G(k) and irreducible complex ρ of K, (K,ρ) is an s-type if for every smooth irreducible π of G(k), Hom_K(ρ,π|K)≠0 iff π belongs to R^s(G).

items.name: Type Hecke algebra
items.statement: Let k be a nonarchimedean local field of residue characteristic p, G a connected reductive k-group split by a tame extension, and p∤|W_abs(G)|. For compact open K and finite-dimensional irreducible ρ, use compactly supported End(ρ)-valued bi-equivariant functions with convolution, in the convention for which Hom_K(ρ,V) is a unital LEFT module. State the opposite-endomorphism-algebra comparison explicitly.

items.name: Type controls its Bernstein block
items.statement: Let k be a nonarchimedean local field of residue characteristic p, G a connected reductive k-group split by a tame extension, and p∤|W_abs(G)|. For an s-type (K,ρ), the functor V↦Hom_K(ρ,V) identifies R^s(G) with unital left modules over the type Hecke algebra in the fixed convention.

items.name: Reductive algebraic-group data
items.statement: Use a smooth geometrically connected reductive affine group over k, its maximal tori, root/coroot datum, derived subgroup, center and parabolic Levi subgroups. Rational points, group schemes and Lie algebras remain different carriers.

items.name: Enlarged building and connected parahoric
items.statement: Let k be a nonarchimedean local field of residue characteristic p, G a connected reductive k-group split by a tame extension, and p∤|W_abs(G)|. Use the enlarged Bruhat–Tits building B(G,k), apartments, facets and connected parahoric G_x,0, with pro-unipotent radical G_x,0+ and finite reductive quotient G_x(f). Retain the projection to the reduced building and both stabilizers.

items.name: Real and right-limit depths
items.statement: Use R together with formal r+ indices, ordered by r<r+<s<s+ when r<s. At a right-limit index the filtration is the union of strictly deeper real levels; group levels are nonnegative while Lie and dual levels range over all real numbers.

items.name: Moy–Prasad filtrations
items.statement: Let k be a nonarchimedean local field of residue characteristic p, G a connected reductive k-group split by a tame extension, and p∤|W_abs(G)|. Construct G_x,r, g_x,r and g*_x,r. The dual lattice at real r consists of X taking g_x,(-r)+ into P and g_x,-r into o. Positive-depth group quotients in the permitted range compare with Lie quotients; all constructions are equivariant in x.

items.name: Conductor-P character
items.statement: Let k be a nonarchimedean local field of residue characteristic p, G a connected reductive k-group split by a tame extension, and p∤|W_abs(G)|. Fix a continuous additive character φ:k→C× which is trivial on the maximal ideal P and nontrivial on o. Pair X in a dual lattice with a Lie quotient to obtain the character Z↦φ(X(Z)); verify representative independence.

items.name: Tame lattice descent
items.statement: Let k be a nonarchimedean local field of residue characteristic p, G a connected reductive k-group split by a tame extension, and p∤|W_abs(G)|. For tame E/k with the extended base valuation, (g_E)_x,r∩g=g_x,r and the analogous dual comparison hold for x∈B(G,k); graded and root decompositions descend with their Galois actions.

items.name: Pointwise and global functional depth
items.statement: Let k be a nonarchimedean local field of residue characteristic p, G a connected reductive k-group split by a tame extension, and p∤|W_abs(G)|. For nonzero X∈g*, d_E(x,X) is the largest r with X∈(g*_E)_x,r and d_E(X)=sup_{x∈B(G,E)}d_E(x,X). Set the depth of zero to +∞. Do not form a finite-depth graded reduction of zero.

items.name: Semistability of a graded vector
items.statement: For a rational representation of a reductive group over the finite residue field, a nonzero vector is semistable if zero is not in the geometric closure of its orbit. This does not assert that the orbit itself is closed.

items.name: Almost stable functional
items.statement: Let k be a nonarchimedean local field of residue characteristic p, G a connected reductive k-group split by a tame extension, and p∤|W_abs(G)|. A functional X∈g* is almost stable if its G(kbar)-coadjoint orbit is closed in the geometric dual Lie algebra. This is a geometric closed-orbit condition.

items.name: Almost strongly stable at a point
items.statement: Let k be a nonarchimedean local field of residue characteristic p, G a connected reductive k-group split by a tame extension, and p∤|W_abs(G)|. For nonzero X of finite depth r at x, X is almost strongly stable at x when it is almost stable and its nonzero image in g*_x,r/g*_x,r+ is semistable under the reductive quotient. The zero/infinite-depth convention is handled separately.

items.name: Almost strong stability attains global depth
items.statement: Let k be a nonarchimedean local field of residue characteristic p, G a connected reductive k-group split by a tame extension, and p∤|W_abs(G)|. If X≠0 is almost strongly stable at x, then d(x,X)=d(X).

items.name: Twisted Levi subgroup
items.statement: For a connected reductive k-group G, a smooth closed k-subgroup G' is a twisted Levi if it becomes a parabolic Levi subgroup after a finite extension. It need not be a Levi of a k-parabolic.

items.name: Closed-orbit centralizer is a twisted Levi
items.statement: Let k be a nonarchimedean local field of residue characteristic p, G a connected reductive k-group split by a tame extension, and p∤|W_abs(G)|. For almost stable X∈g*, Cent_G(X) is a twisted Levi subgroup. The proof requires the invariant bilinear identification and prime-to-p saturation of the coroot kernel; connectedness is not assumed for an arbitrary centralizer.

items.name: Weyl-order bound passes to Levis
items.statement: Let k be a nonarchimedean local field of residue characteristic p, G a connected reductive k-group split by a tame extension, and p∤|W_abs(G)|. The residue prime p does not divide the Weyl-group order of any twisted Levi subgroup.

items.name: Root bond-order bound
items.statement: Let k be a nonarchimedean local field of residue characteristic p, G a connected reductive k-group split by a tame extension, and p∤|W_abs(G)|. The prime p is strictly greater than every bond order in the root system (the squared long/short root-length ratio).

items.name: Good prime for coroots
items.statement: Let k be a nonarchimedean local field of residue characteristic p, G a connected reductive k-group split by a tame extension, and p∤|W_abs(G)|. The prime p is not a bad prime for the coroot system of G.

items.name: No root or dual torsion primes
items.statement: Let k be a nonarchimedean local field of residue characteristic p, G a connected reductive k-group split by a tame extension, and p∤|W_abs(G)|. The prime p is not a torsion prime for either the root system or its dual.

items.name: Parabolic-subsystem connection indices
items.statement: Let k be a nonarchimedean local field of residue characteristic p, G a connected reductive k-group split by a tame extension, and p∤|W_abs(G)|. The prime p divides no index of connection of a parabolic root subsystem.

items.name: All maximal tori are tame
items.statement: Let k be a nonarchimedean local field of residue characteristic p, G a connected reductive k-group split by a tame extension, and p∤|W_abs(G)|. Every maximal k-torus of G splits over a tame extension. This is the sufficient direction imported from Fin19; no general converse for all inner forms is inferred.

items.name: Lattice-compatible invariant bilinear form
items.statement: Let k be a nonarchimedean local field of residue characteristic p, G a connected reductive k-group split by a tame extension, and p∤|W_abs(G)|. Construct a G-invariant nondegenerate symmetric bilinear form B on g, identifying g_x,r with g*_x,r for every x,r and remaining nondegenerate on the Lie algebra of every twisted Levi. Track the normalization of root vectors/coroots in this comparison.

items.name: Centralizer root-system saturation
items.statement: Let k be a nonarchimedean local field of residue characteristic p, G a connected reductive k-group split by a tame extension, and p∤|W_abs(G)|. For a semisimple dual element under B and a split maximal torus T in its centralizer, the vanishing coroot values define the centralizer root subsystem; prime-to-p lattice saturation gives the Levi and connectedness conclusions used in Lemma3.4. The general closed-subgroup and root constructions remain upstream.

items.name: Generic functional of a specified depth
items.statement: Let k be a nonarchimedean local field of residue characteristic p, G a connected reductive k-group split by a tame extension, and p∤|W_abs(G)|. X is generic of real depth r at x if its geometric orbit is closed, a maximal torus of Cent_G(X) splits over tame E with x in its apartment, X∈g*_x,r, and each coroot value X(Hα) is zero or has valuation r. If all coroot values vanish, also require d(x,X)=r.

items.name: Generic root values for any centralizer torus
items.statement: Let k be a nonarchimedean local field of residue characteristic p, G a connected reductive k-group split by a tame extension, and p∤|W_abs(G)|. If X is generic of depth r at x, then for every maximal torus T of Cent_G(X), after splitting T, X(Hα)=0 for centralizer roots and val(X(Hα))=r for the remaining roots.

items.name: Generic functional annihilates root spaces
items.statement: Let k be a nonarchimedean local field of residue characteristic p, G a connected reductive k-group split by a tame extension, and p∤|W_abs(G)|. For X generic as above and a split maximal torus T of its centralizer, X vanishes on every root space of g_E relative to T.

items.name: Generic depth equals global depth
items.statement: Let k be a nonarchimedean local field of residue characteristic p, G a connected reductive k-group split by a tame extension, and p∤|W_abs(G)|. For nonzero X generic of depth r at x, d(x,X)=d(X)=r.

items.name: Generic implies almost strongly stable
items.statement: Let k be a nonarchimedean local field of residue characteristic p, G a connected reductive k-group split by a tame extension, and p∤|W_abs(G)|. A nonzero generic functional is almost strongly stable at its specified point.

items.name: Rational destabilizing cocharacter
items.statement: For a reductive group over a perfect field and a rational vector whose geometric orbit closure contains zero, obtain a cocharacter defined over the base field contracting that vector to zero, in the setting of Kempf Corollary4.3. The application is over the finite residue field; the local field itself need not be perfect.

items.name: Lift a residual split torus and cocharacter
items.statement: Let k be a nonarchimedean local field of residue characteristic p, G a connected reductive k-group split by a tame extension, and p∤|W_abs(G)|. Given the residual reductive quotient at x and a split torus containing a residual cocharacter, lift it through the smooth parahoric to a k-split torus lying in a suitable tame maximal torus whose apartment contains x. Compare the residual weights with affine-root movement at x.

items.name: Tame twisted-Levi building image
items.statement: Let k be a nonarchimedean local field of residue characteristic p, G a connected reductive k-group split by a tame extension, and p∤|W_abs(G)|. A tame twisted Levi G' has an embedding B(G',k)→B(G,k), determined up to the stated central translations; its image is canonical. Obtain it by tame Galois descent and make the apartment/root-filtration compatibility explicit.

items.name: Generic depth drops off the centralizer building
items.statement: Let k be a nonarchimedean local field of residue characteristic p, G a connected reductive k-group split by a tame extension, and p∤|W_abs(G)|. If X is nonzero generic of depth r, G'=Cent_G(X), X' lies in the global union (g')*_(r+), and y∉B(G',k), then d(y,X+X')<d(X). The dual of g' is embedded using B. The KM03 characteristic-zero proof needs the AR00-compatible equal-characteristic justification used here.

items.name: Deeper coroot projection
items.statement: Let k be a nonarchimedean local field of residue characteristic p, G a connected reductive k-group split by a tame extension, and p∤|W_abs(G)|. For almost strongly stable X of depth r, choose a maximal torus in Cent_G(X) and form the coroot subsystem on which val(X(Hα))>r. Split its coroot span from the common annihilator, extend by root spaces, and project X to a Galois-invariant deeper functional X'. Prime-to-p connection indices control all denominators.

items.name: Arbitrarily close generic approximation
items.statement: Let k be a nonarchimedean local field of residue characteristic p, G a connected reductive k-group split by a tame extension, and p∤|W_abs(G)|. If nonzero X is almost strongly stable at x of depth r, then for every ε>0 there are x' with d(x,x')<ε and generic Xtilde of depth r at x', with Xtilde−X∈g*_x',r+ and both x,x'∈B(Cent_G(Xtilde),k). The congruence is at x', not necessarily at x.

items.name: Root-bounded building metric
items.statement: Let k be a nonarchimedean local field of residue characteristic p, G a connected reductive k-group split by a tame extension, and p∤|W_abs(G)|. Fix a G(k)-invariant metric on the enlarged building, compatible with the tame apartment embeddings, scaled so that |α(x−y)|≤d(x,y) for every relevant root and same-apartment x,y.

items.name: Residual reductive action on graded Lie pieces
items.statement: Let k be a nonarchimedean local field of residue characteristic p, G a connected reductive k-group split by a tame extension, and p∤|W_abs(G)|. At x, construct the finite-dimensional residue-field spaces g_x,r/g_x,r+ and their duals with the action of the connected reductive quotient G_x. Identify the dual grading under the conductor-P pairing.

items.name: Almost-stable representative in a dual coset
items.statement: Let k be a nonarchimedean local field of residue characteristic p, G a connected reductive k-group split by a tame extension, and p∤|W_abs(G)|. Every deeper-lattice coset occurring in the definition of the §6 minimum-depth function contains an almost stable representative, by the invariant-form/semisimple representative argument cited there. This input requires its own source proof; it is not furnished by the existence of B alone.

items.name: Degenerate cosets yield unstable leading terms
items.statement: Let k be a nonarchimedean local field of residue characteristic p, G a connected reductive k-group split by a tame extension, and p∤|W_abs(G)|. Use the Adler–DeBacker degenerate-coset criterion and Moy–Prasad results to show that a functional whose depth can be increased globally has unstable leading reduction at a point of smaller depth. This is the exact contrapositive needed by Lemma3.2, not an arbitrary equivalence for every representation.

items.name: Extended functional datum
items.statement: Let k be a nonarchimedean local field of residue characteristic p, G a connected reductive k-group split by a tame extension, and p∤|W_abs(G)|. A length n≥0 extended datum consists of x, strictly decreasing positive r_1>…>r_n, X_i of depth −r_i, G=G_1⊇G_2⊋…⊋G_{n+1}, and an irreducible representation ρ_0 of (G_{n+1}^der)_x,0/(G_{n+1}^der)_x,0+. Require x∈B(G_{n+1},k), X_i∈g_i* embedded by B, X_i G_i-generic at x, and G_{i+1}=Cent_{G_i}(X_i). For n=0 keep x,G and ρ_0.

items.name: Truncated extended datum
items.statement: Let k be a nonarchimedean local field of residue characteristic p, G a connected reductive k-group split by a tame extension, and p∤|W_abs(G)|. A truncated extended datum is the preceding tuple with ρ_0 omitted, retaining x, r_i, X_i and G_i and every genericity and strictness condition.

items.name: Functional datum
items.statement: Let k be a nonarchimedean local field of residue characteristic p, G a connected reductive k-group split by a tame extension, and p∤|W_abs(G)|. A datum is (x,(X_i)_{1≤i≤n},ρ_0) which admits the extended datum of Definition4.1. The depths and groups are uniquely recovered. The finite quotient can equivalently be written using Cent_G(ΣX_i)^der∩G_x,0 and its intersection with G_x,0+.

items.name: Truncated functional datum
items.statement: Let k be a nonarchimedean local field of residue characteristic p, G a connected reductive k-group split by a tame extension, and p∤|W_abs(G)|. A truncated datum is (x,(X_i)) admitting a truncated extended datum; omit only the depth-zero representation, not the genericity conditions.

items.name: Recover the terminal centralizer
items.statement: Let k be a nonarchimedean local field of residue characteristic p, G a connected reductive k-group split by a tame extension, and p∤|W_abs(G)|. For an extended datum, the successive centralizer chain and the distinct generic depths identify G_{n+1}=Cent_G(Σ_i X_i); recover r_i=−d(x,X_i). This supplies the uniqueness assertion and the quotient used in Definition4.2.

items.name: Move a truncated datum within the last building
items.statement: Let k be a nonarchimedean local field of residue characteristic p, G a connected reductive k-group split by a tame extension, and p∤|W_abs(G)|. If (x,(X_i)) is a truncated datum and y∈B(G_{n+1},k), then (y,(X_i)) is a truncated datum with the same recovered depths and groups.

items.name: Derived auxiliary chain
items.statement: Let k be a nonarchimedean local field of residue characteristic p, G a connected reductive k-group split by a tame extension, and p∤|W_abs(G)|. For a datum set H_1=G_1 if G_1=G_2 and otherwise H_1=G_1^der; for i>1 set H_i=G_i^der. In the length-zero case H_{n+1}=G^der. Use H_i(k)∩G_x,r for its filtration, compared with the image of x in B(H_i,k).

items.name: Mixed-depth Levi-pair groups
items.statement: Let k be a nonarchimedean local field of residue characteristic p, G a connected reductive k-group split by a tame extension, and p∤|W_abs(G)|. For successive G_i⊇G_{i+1}, a tame split maximal T in G_{i+1} with x in its apartment, and indices a≥b≥a/2>0, define (G_i)_x,a,b as the k-points in the subgroup generated by T(E)_a, G_i-root groups at depth a, and root groups outside G_{i+1} at depth b. Set (H_i)_x,a,b=H_i(k)∩(G_i)_x,a,b and define the corresponding Lie lattices.

items.name: Containment of a datum
items.statement: Let k be a nonarchimedean local field of residue characteristic p, G a connected reductive k-group split by a tame extension, and p∤|W_abs(G)|. A datum is contained in smooth irreducible π when a subspace V' fixed by every (H_i)_x,r_i+ (1≤i≤n+1, r_{n+1}=0) restricts to ρ_0 under (H_{n+1})_x,0 and each mixed quotient (H_i)_x,r_i,(r_i/2)+/(H_i)_x,r_i+ acts on it by φ∘X_i.

items.name: Containment of a truncated datum
items.statement: Let k be a nonarchimedean local field of residue characteristic p, G a connected reductive k-group split by a tame extension, and p∤|W_abs(G)|. A truncated datum is contained in smooth irreducible π if there is a nonzero line fixed by (H_i)_x,r_i+ for 1≤i≤n on which all mixed quotients at (r_i,(r_i/2)+) act by φ∘X_i.

items.name: Facet-maximal contained datum
items.statement: Let k be a nonarchimedean local field of residue characteristic p, G a connected reductive k-group split by a tame extension, and p∤|W_abs(G)|. A contained datum is maximal when the dimension of the facet containing x in its terminal-Levi building is maximal among contained data, comparing each competing point in its own recovered terminal-Levi building. Record the unprimed comparison notation in Definition4.6 as source issue E1.

items.name: Off-centralizer root complement
items.statement: Let k be a nonarchimedean local field of residue characteristic p, G a connected reductive k-group split by a tame extension, and p∤|W_abs(G)|. For nonzero X generic of depth −r at x and G'=Cent_G(X), choose tame split maximal T in G'. Write g=t⊕r'⊕r'' with r' the G'-root spaces and r'' the remaining root spaces, descended to k; let j* be the annihilator of g'.

items.name: Generic bracket pairing is an isomorphism
items.statement: Let k be a nonarchimedean local field of residue characteristic p, G a connected reductive k-group split by a tame extension, and p∤|W_abs(G)|. For the Lemma5.1 setup with r>0, Y↦(Z↦X([Y,Z])) identifies r'' linearly with j*.

items.name: Bracket pairing shifts depth by −r
items.statement: Let k be a nonarchimedean local field of residue characteristic p, G a connected reductive k-group split by a tame extension, and p∤|W_abs(G)|. For that isomorphism f_X and every real s, f_X(r''∩g_x,s)=j*∩g*_x,s−r.

items.name: Positive-depth mock exponential
items.statement: Let k be a nonarchimedean local field of residue characteristic p, G a connected reductive k-group split by a tame extension, and p∤|W_abs(G)|. For positive s and an off-Levi root vector Y=ΣaαXα in g_x,s, construct a k-rational mock exponential agreeing modulo G(E)_x,2s with the ordered product of root elements xα(aα). Prove Ad(exp Y)Z≡Z+[Y,Z] modulo depth t+2s for Z of depth t.

items.name: Remove perturbation on the depth-r lattice
items.statement: Let k be a nonarchimedean local field of residue characteristic p, G a connected reductive k-group split by a tame extension, and p∤|W_abs(G)|. Let r>0, X generic of depth −r at x, G'=Cent_G(X), r/2≤d<r, 0<ε<(r−d)/2, and C∈j*∩g*_x,−(d+ε). There is g∈G_x,r−d−ε such that Ad(g)(X+C)|g_x,r=X|g_x,r. The same g works for the next two assertions.

items.name: Remove the off-Levi deeper restriction
items.statement: Let k be a nonarchimedean local field of residue characteristic p, G a connected reductive k-group split by a tame extension, and p∤|W_abs(G)|. Let r>0, X generic of depth −r at x, G'=Cent_G(X), r/2≤d<r, 0<ε<(r−d)/2, and C∈j*∩g*_x,−(d+ε). For the g constructed in Lemma5.1(b), Ad(g)(X+C) and X both vanish on r''∩g_x,d+.

items.name: Preserve the deeper centralizer action
items.statement: Let k be a nonarchimedean local field of residue characteristic p, G a connected reductive k-group split by a tame extension, and p∤|W_abs(G)|. Let r>0, X generic of depth −r at x, G'=Cent_G(X), r/2≤d<r, 0<ε<(r−d)/2, and C∈j*∩g*_x,−(d+ε). Suppose V' in a G(k)-representation is killed by the k-rational subgroup generated by T(E)_r+, outside-G' roots at (d+ε)+ and G' roots at r+. If H⊂G'^der(k)∩G_x,(2d−r+2ε)+ stabilizes V', then g^{-1}Hg preserves V' and the conjugated H-action agrees with the original one.

items.name: One-step correction preserves fixed vectors
items.statement: Let k be a nonarchimedean local field of residue characteristic p, G a connected reductive k-group split by a tame extension, and p∤|W_abs(G)|. Let a length-n truncated datum and 1≤j≤n be fixed. Take r_j/2≤d<r_j and 0<ε<(r_j−d)/2. Let nonzero V' be fixed by all (H_i)_x,r_i+ for i≤j, have the prescribed mixed scalar actions for i<j, and have (H_j)_x,r_j−ε,d+/(H_j)_x,r_j+ act via φ∘(X_j+C), where C∈(h_j)*_x,−(d+ε) annihilates t_j+h_{j+1}. There exists g∈(H_j)_x,r_j−d−ε for which V''=π(g)V' remains fixed by all (H_i)_x,r_i+ (i≤j). Use this same g in the other three conclusions.

items.name: One-step correction preserves earlier characters
items.statement: Let k be a nonarchimedean local field of residue characteristic p, G a connected reductive k-group split by a tame extension, and p∤|W_abs(G)|. Let a length-n truncated datum and 1≤j≤n be fixed. Take r_j/2≤d<r_j and 0<ε<(r_j−d)/2. Let nonzero V' be fixed by all (H_i)_x,r_i+ for i≤j, have the prescribed mixed scalar actions for i<j, and have (H_j)_x,r_j−ε,d+/(H_j)_x,r_j+ act via φ∘(X_j+C), where C∈(h_j)*_x,−(d+ε) annihilates t_j+h_{j+1}. The V'' constructed in Corollary5.2 retains the φ∘X_i mixed actions for every i<j.

items.name: One-step correction removes the current character error
items.statement: Let k be a nonarchimedean local field of residue characteristic p, G a connected reductive k-group split by a tame extension, and p∤|W_abs(G)|. Let a length-n truncated datum and 1≤j≤n be fixed. Take r_j/2≤d<r_j and 0<ε<(r_j−d)/2. Let nonzero V' be fixed by all (H_i)_x,r_i+ for i≤j, have the prescribed mixed scalar actions for i<j, and have (H_j)_x,r_j−ε,d+/(H_j)_x,r_j+ act via φ∘(X_j+C), where C∈(h_j)*_x,−(d+ε) annihilates t_j+h_{j+1}. On V'', the quotient (H_j)_x,r_j,d+/(H_j)_x,r_j+ acts by φ∘X_j.

items.name: One-step correction preserves terminal representations
items.statement: Let k be a nonarchimedean local field of residue characteristic p, G a connected reductive k-group split by a tame extension, and p∤|W_abs(G)|. Let a length-n truncated datum and 1≤j≤n be fixed. Take r_j/2≤d<r_j and 0<ε<(r_j−d)/2. Let nonzero V' be fixed by all (H_i)_x,r_i+ for i≤j, have the prescribed mixed scalar actions for i<j, and have (H_j)_x,r_j−ε,d+/(H_j)_x,r_j+ act via φ∘(X_j+C), where C∈(h_j)*_x,−(d+ε) annihilates t_j+h_{j+1}. Every H⊂(H_{j+1})_x,(2d−r_j+2ε)+ stabilizing V' also stabilizes V'', and the two H-representations are isomorphic.

items.name: Simultaneous correction preserves fixed spaces
items.statement: Let k be a nonarchimedean local field of residue characteristic p, G a connected reductive k-group split by a tame extension, and p∤|W_abs(G)|. Let n>0, a truncated datum and 0<ε<r_n/4 satisfy (H_i)_x,r_i−ε,(r_i/2)+=(H_i)_x,r_i,(r_i/2)+ for all i. Let nonzero V' be fixed by all (H_i)_x,r_i+ and carry mixed characters φ∘(X_i+C_i), where C_i∈(h_i)*_x,−(r_i/2+ε) annihilates (t∩h_i)+h_{i+1}. Successive one-step corrections give g∈G_x,r_n/2−ε such that V''=π(g)V' remains fixed by all (H_i)_x,r_i+.

items.name: Simultaneous correction removes all character errors
items.statement: Let k be a nonarchimedean local field of residue characteristic p, G a connected reductive k-group split by a tame extension, and p∤|W_abs(G)|. Let n>0, a truncated datum and 0<ε<r_n/4 satisfy (H_i)_x,r_i−ε,(r_i/2)+=(H_i)_x,r_i,(r_i/2)+ for all i. Let nonzero V' be fixed by all (H_i)_x,r_i+ and carry mixed characters φ∘(X_i+C_i), where C_i∈(h_i)*_x,−(r_i/2+ε) annihilates (t∩h_i)+h_{i+1}. The same V'' has every prescribed mixed action φ∘X_i for 1≤i≤n.

items.name: Simultaneous correction preserves deeper terminal action
items.statement: Let k be a nonarchimedean local field of residue characteristic p, G a connected reductive k-group split by a tame extension, and p∤|W_abs(G)|. Let n>0, a truncated datum and 0<ε<r_n/4 satisfy (H_i)_x,r_i−ε,(r_i/2)+=(H_i)_x,r_i,(r_i/2)+ for all i. Let nonzero V' be fixed by all (H_i)_x,r_i+ and carry mixed characters φ∘(X_i+C_i), where C_i∈(h_i)*_x,−(r_i/2+ε) annihilates (t∩h_i)+h_{i+1}. If H⊂(H_{n+1})_x,2ε+ stabilizes V', it also stabilizes V'', with isomorphic H-actions.

items.name: Extend the last depth character to its mixed group
items.statement: Let k be a nonarchimedean local field of residue characteristic p, G a connected reductive k-group split by a tame extension, and p∤|W_abs(G)|. Let n>0 and a truncated datum be given, with 0<ε<r_n/4 and (H_n)_x,r_n−2ε=(H_n)_x,r_n. If nonzero V' is fixed by all (H_i)_x,r_i+, carries the prescribed mixed characters for i<n, and carries φ∘X_n on (H_n)_x,r_n/(H_n)_x,r_n+, then π has a nonzero subspace carrying every prescribed mixed character and fixed by all the deeper groups. Repeated one-step corrections terminate at half depth.

items.name: Residual minimum-depth function
items.statement: Let k be a nonarchimedean local field of residue characteristic p, G a connected reductive k-group split by a tame extension, and p∤|W_abs(G)|. During the length-(j−1) recursion, f(y) is the least r≥0 for which the previous truncated datum at y remains contained and a nonzero compatible subspace, fixed by (H_j)_y,r+, carries at r>0 a graded character represented by an almost stable X_j∈(g_j)*_y,−r. Set f(y)=∞ if none exists. At j=1 this is the ordinary representation depth at y.

items.name: Residual depth is terminal-Levi invariant
items.statement: Let k be a nonarchimedean local field of residue characteristic p, G a connected reductive k-group split by a tame extension, and p∤|W_abs(G)|. For the §6 recursion, f(g.y)=f(y) for g∈G_j(k).

items.name: Finite-depth locus is open
items.statement: Let k be a nonarchimedean local field of residue characteristic p, G a connected reductive k-group split by a tame extension, and p∤|W_abs(G)|. For the §6 recursion, f^{-1}(R≥0) is open in B(G_j,k). Nearby filtration comparisons and simultaneous correction preserve a finite bound.

items.name: Residual depth is continuous on its finite locus
items.statement: Let k be a nonarchimedean local field of residue characteristic p, G a connected reductive k-group split by a tame extension, and p∤|W_abs(G)|. The function f is continuous on f^{-1}(R≥0); in the positive-depth case use the two-sided |f(y)−f(x)|≤ε argument, and at zero use nonnegativity and arbitrarily small upper bounds.

items.name: Every point has finite residual depth
items.statement: Let k be a nonarchimedean local field of residue characteristic p, G a connected reductive k-group split by a tame extension, and p∤|W_abs(G)|. The finite-depth locus is closed, using a uniform small gap between nearby filtration jumps; it is nonempty and open, hence all of the connected building B(G_j,k).

items.name: Residual depth has a global minimum
items.statement: Let k be a nonarchimedean local field of residue characteristic p, G a connected reductive k-group split by a tame extension, and p∤|W_abs(G)|. The finite continuous G_j(k)-invariant function f attains its infimum on B(G_j,k), using a compact fundamental region modulo the central-translation action. Thus choose x_j with r_j=f(x_j)≤f(x_{j−1}).

items.name: A positive minimal-depth representative is strongly stable
items.statement: Let k be a nonarchimedean local field of residue characteristic p, G a connected reductive k-group split by a tame extension, and p∤|W_abs(G)|. If r_j=f(x_j)>0 and X_j is a compatible almost stable representative, its leading reduction is semistable. Otherwise lift a rational destabilizing cocharacter, move x_j slightly, and use simultaneous correction to produce depth below the minimum.

items.name: Extend the contained truncated datum
items.statement: Let k be a nonarchimedean local field of residue characteristic p, G a connected reductive k-group split by a tame extension, and p∤|W_abs(G)|. At a positive minimum choose nearby y and generic Xtilde by Proposition3.12; preserve previous characters by Corollary5.3 and extend the last action by Corollary5.4. This yields a length-j contained truncated datum with the strictly descending depth/centralizer conditions. Prove those strict inequalities explicitly, including j=2.

items.name: Centralizer descent terminates
items.statement: Let k be a nonarchimedean local field of residue characteristic p, G a connected reductive k-group split by a tame extension, and p∤|W_abs(G)|. The recursion cannot extend indefinitely: after the possible first equal step G_1=G_2, every further terminal centralizer is proper, so its dimension decreases. The finite procedure reaches residual depth zero.

items.name: Complete at residual depth zero
items.statement: Let k be a nonarchimedean local field of residue characteristic p, G a connected reductive k-group split by a tame extension, and p∤|W_abs(G)|. At r_j=0 choose a nonzero irreducible constituent of the finite derived-parahoric quotient on the compatible subspace, obtaining ρ_0 and a contained datum. Existence follows from finite-group complete reducibility over C.

items.name: Every irreducible contains a datum
items.statement: Let k be a nonarchimedean local field of residue characteristic p, G a connected reductive k-group split by a tame extension, and p∤|W_abs(G)|. Every smooth irreducible complex representation π of G(k) contains a datum in the sense of Definition4.5.

items.name: Existence of a maximal datum
items.statement: Let k be a nonarchimedean local field of residue characteristic p, G a connected reductive k-group split by a tame extension, and p∤|W_abs(G)|. Every smooth irreducible π has a maximal datum: combine datum existence with bounded integral facet dimensions.

items.name: Levi attached to a parahoric facet
items.statement: Let k be a nonarchimedean local field of residue characteristic p, G a connected reductive k-group split by a tame extension, and p∤|W_abs(G)|. For x in B(G_{n+1},k), construct the k-Levi M_{n+1} used by MP96 §§6.3–6.4: x lies in its building, (M_{n+1})_x,0 is a maximal parahoric there, and its reductive quotient identifies with that of (G_{n+1})_x,0.

items.name: Terminal compact subgroup
items.statement: Let k be a nonarchimedean local field of residue characteristic p, G a connected reductive k-group split by a tame extension, and p∤|W_abs(G)|. Let K_{G_{n+1}} be generated by the stabilizer of x in M_{n+1}(k) and (G_{n+1})_x,0. This is the compact subgroup used for types; replacing the stabilizer of x by that of [x] in the reduced building is a separate later construction.

items.name: Choose a compatible compact-group constituent
items.statement: Let k be a nonarchimedean local field of residue characteristic p, G a connected reductive k-group split by a tame extension, and p∤|W_abs(G)|. From the nonzero datum-character subspace choose a compatible irreducible K_{G_{n+1}} constituent and later a compatible K constituent by an equivariant nonzero projection, adjusting the witness subspace if necessary. Do not assert that an arbitrary fixed smaller-group irreducible subspace lies inside a larger-group irreducible subspace.
items.locator: §7 p26; before Lemma7.8 p31; source issue E5

items.name: Positive-depth torus acts by a scalar character
items.statement: Let k be a nonarchimedean local field of residue characteristic p, G a connected reductive k-group split by a tame extension, and p∤|W_abs(G)|. For the compatible irreducible K_{G_{n+1}} representation Vtilde and maximal T⊂M_{n+1} with x in its apartment, T(k)_0+ acts by one character φ_T. Its commutators with K_{G_{n+1}} lie in (H_{n+1})_x,0+, which acts trivially.

items.name: Positive-depth tame torus exactness
items.statement: If 1→A→B→C→1 is an exact sequence of k-tori all split by a tame extension of the nonarchimedean local field k, then for every r>0, 1→A(k)_r→B(k)_r→C(k)_r→1 is exact. No depth-zero version is claimed.

items.name: Generate a positive-depth group by torus and derived group
items.statement: Let k be a nonarchimedean local field of residue characteristic p, G a connected reductive k-group split by a tame extension, and p∤|W_abs(G)|. For 1≤j≤n+1 and real r>0, (G_j)_x,r is generated by T(k)_r and (H_j)_x,r for the torus fixed in §7.

items.name: Extend continuous characters of an abelian quotient
items.statement: For the locally compact abelian torus quotient in §7, a continuous character on the stated open positive-depth subgroup extends to the whole quotient. The extension is generally not canonical. Export restriction and triviality after pullback to G_j(k).

items.name: Generic positive-depth group character
items.statement: Let k be a nonarchimedean local field of residue characteristic p, G a connected reductive k-group split by a tame extension, and p∤|W_abs(G)|. For G_i⊇G_{i+1}, a G_i-generic character φ_i of G_{i+1}(k) relative to x has depth r_i and the Yu genericity conditions represented on the graded quotient by a central functional with coroot values of valuation −r_i on roots outside G_{i+1}. The Weyl-stabilizer condition is a separate conclusion of the prime hypotheses, not omitted.

items.name: Construct the sequence of generic characters
items.statement: Let k be a nonarchimedean local field of residue characteristic p, G a connected reductive k-group split by a tame extension, and p∤|W_abs(G)|. Construct φ_n,…,φ_1 in reverse order from φ_T. At step j extend the residual torus character through G_{j+1}/H_{j+1}, subtract an extension through G_j/H_j to kill depths beyond r_j, and choose that second extension trivial for j=1. Keep all extension choices and restriction compatibilities.

items.name: Generic character is trivial above its depth
items.statement: Let k be a nonarchimedean local field of residue characteristic p, G a connected reductive k-group split by a tame extension, and p∤|W_abs(G)|. Each constructed φ_j is trivial on (G_{j+1})_x,r_j+.

items.name: Generic character kills the next derived group
items.statement: Let k be a nonarchimedean local field of residue characteristic p, G a connected reductive k-group split by a tame extension, and p∤|W_abs(G)|. Each constructed φ_j is trivial on H_{j+1}(k).

items.name: Generic character realizes the functional
items.statement: Let k be a nonarchimedean local field of residue characteristic p, G a connected reductive k-group split by a tame extension, and p∤|W_abs(G)|. The restriction of φ_j to (H_j)_x,r_j∩G_{j+1}(k) factors through the quotient by (H_j)_x,r_j+∩G_{j+1}(k), and under the group–Lie comparison is φ∘X_j on the corresponding Lie intersection.

items.name: Constructed character is Yu-generic
items.statement: Let k be a nonarchimedean local field of residue characteristic p, G a connected reductive k-group split by a tame extension, and p∤|W_abs(G)|. The constructed φ_j is G_j-generic of exact depth r_j relative to x. Retain the relative-to-x correction to KY17 D5 noted in footnote2.

items.name: Product character on the terminal pro-unipotent group
items.statement: Let k be a nonarchimedean local field of residue characteristic p, G a connected reductive k-group split by a tame extension, and p∤|W_abs(G)|. On Vtilde the action of (G_{n+1})_x,0+ is the scalar product ∏_{i=1}^n φ_i.

items.name: Untwist to depth zero without assuming cuspidality
items.statement: Let k be a nonarchimedean local field of residue characteristic p, G a connected reductive k-group split by a tame extension, and p∤|W_abs(G)|. The irreducible K_{G_{n+1}} representation (∏φ_i^{-1})⊗Vtilde is trivial on (G_{n+1})_x,0+ and its restriction to (H_{n+1})_x,0 contains ρ_0.

items.name: Type group and positive-depth subgroups
items.statement: Let k be a nonarchimedean local field of residue characteristic p, G a connected reductive k-group split by a tame extension, and p∤|W_abs(G)|. Define K=K_{G_{n+1}}(G_n)_x,r_n/2⋯(G_1)_x,r_1/2, K_0+=(G_{n+1})_x,0+(G_n)_x,r_n/2⋯(G_1)_x,r_1/2 and K_+=(G_{n+1})_x,0+(G_n)_x,(r_n/2)+⋯(G_1)_x,(r_1/2)+. For n=0 the products are empty.

items.name: Derived positive-depth type subgroups
items.statement: Let k be a nonarchimedean local field of residue characteristic p, G a connected reductive k-group split by a tame extension, and p∤|W_abs(G)|. Define K_0+^H=(H_{n+1})_x,0+(H_n)_x,r_n/2⋯(H_1)_x,r_1/2 and K_+^H with every half-depth index replaced by its plus index. Preserve H_1's possible nonderived exception.

items.name: Factor K_+ through the derived chain
items.statement: Let k be a nonarchimedean local field of residue characteristic p, G a connected reductive k-group split by a tame extension, and p∤|W_abs(G)|. For the §7 groups, K_+=(G_{n+1})_x,0+ K_+^H.

items.name: Factor K_0+ through the derived chain
items.statement: Let k be a nonarchimedean local field of residue characteristic p, G a connected reductive k-group split by a tame extension, and p∤|W_abs(G)|. For the §7 groups, K_0+=(G_{n+1})_x,0+ K_0+^H.

items.name: Mixed-depth expression for K_0+^H
items.statement: Let k be a nonarchimedean local field of residue characteristic p, G a connected reductive k-group split by a tame extension, and p∤|W_abs(G)|. For the §7 groups, K_0+^H=(H_{n+1})_x,0+(H_n)_x,r_n,r_n/2⋯(H_1)_x,r_1,r_1/2.

items.name: Mixed-depth expression for K_+^H
items.statement: Let k be a nonarchimedean local field of residue characteristic p, G a connected reductive k-group split by a tame extension, and p∤|W_abs(G)|. For the §7 groups, K_+^H=(H_{n+1})_x,0+(H_n)_x,r_n,(r_n/2)+⋯(H_1)_x,r_1,(r_1/2)+.

items.name: Extended generic character
items.statement: Let k be a nonarchimedean local field of residue characteristic p, G a connected reductive k-group split by a tame extension, and p∤|W_abs(G)|. For each i, let φhat_i be the unique character on K_{G_{n+1}}(G_{i+1})_x,0 G_x,(r_i/2)+ extending φ_i on the first two factors and, on the last, induced through the group–Lie quotient and projection g=g_{i+1}⊕r''→g_{i+1}. Prove the restrictions agree on intersections.

items.name: Finite Heisenberg group
items.statement: For a finite-dimensional symplectic F_p-space V with p odd and alternating nondegenerate pairing ⟨,⟩, define V^sharp=V×F_p with (v,a)(w,b)=(v+w,a+b+⟨v,w⟩/2). Include V=0, in which case the group is the center F_p. Choose μ_p(C)≃(F_p,+) before identifying commutator values.

items.name: Finite Schrödinger representation
items.statement: For V=X⊕X* over F_p with p odd and a fixed nontrivial additive central character, construct the irreducible Heisenberg representation on complex functions on X using translation and modulation with the half-pairing convention. Transport it across polarizations.

items.name: Finite Stone–von Neumann uniqueness
items.statement: For the odd-p finite Heisenberg group attached to a nondegenerate symplectic V and a fixed nontrivial character of its center, every irreducible complex representation with that character is isomorphic to the Schrödinger representation.

items.name: Normalized finite Weil representation
items.statement: For odd p, equip the finite Schrödinger module with the normalized Weil action of Sp(V), compatible with the Heisenberg action, to obtain a representation of Sp(V)⋉V^sharp. Retain the source's normalization, especially on Levi subgroups; a projective action alone is insufficient.

items.name: Corrected finite Weil parabolic restriction
items.statement: For V=V+⊕V0⊕V− with V± isotropic, (V+)⊥=V+⊕V0 and V0 nondegenerate, let P preserve V+. The restriction of the Weil–Heisenberg representation to P⋉V^sharp is induced from P⋉(V+×(V0)^sharp) of the pullback Weil–Heisenberg representation on V0 tensor χ_{V+}, where χ_{V+}(g)=det(g|V+)^{(p−1)/2}. The omitted factor in Gér77 is essential.

items.name: Isotropic invariants with determinant twist
items.statement: Under the preceding decomposition, invariants under V+×0 identify, as a P-representation, with the Weil representation on V0 tensored by χ_{V+}. In particular, if V+ is Lagrangian, these invariants form one line with the determinant character.

items.name: Nonzero unipotent fixed vectors in the needed Weil restriction
items.statement: For the finite p-subgroup obtained from a residual unipotent radical in Lemma7.10, its image in GL(V+) kills χ_{V+}, and its image in Sp(V0) lies in a parabolic stabilizing a maximal isotropic space. The Weil module therefore has a nonzero vector fixed by that group and by V+×0.

items.name: Heisenberg quotient of a generic mixed group
items.statement: Let k be a nonarchimedean local field of residue characteristic p, G a connected reductive k-group split by a tame extension, and p∤|W_abs(G)|. For each i, form J_i=(G_i)_x,r_i,r_i/2 and J_i+=(G_i)_x,r_i,(r_i/2)+. The quotient J_i/(J_i+∩ker φhat_i) is a finite Heisenberg p-group with center J_i+/(J_i+∩ker φhat_i), and commutator pairing on V_i=J_i/J_i+. Construct the special isomorphism to V_i^sharp, not merely an abstract group isomorphism.

items.name: Tensor Heisenberg–Weil factor
items.statement: Let k be a nonarchimedean local field of residue characteristic p, G a connected reductive k-group split by a tame extension, and p∤|W_abs(G)|. Let ω_i be the irreducible representation of the i-th Heisenberg quotient with central character φhat_i. Define V_κ=⊗_i V_{ω_i}; let J_i act by ω_i on its factor and φhat_j on factors j≠i, and let the terminal compact subgroup act through the Weil action times φ_i on each factor. Prove compatibility on subgroup intersections. For n=0 let κ be trivial on C.

items.name: The Heisenberg–Weil factor is irreducible at K_0+
items.statement: Let k be a nonarchimedean local field of residue characteristic p, G a connected reductive k-group split by a tame extension, and p∤|W_abs(G)|. The restriction of κ to K_0+ is irreducible, with tensor product space ⊗V_{ω_i}; use the Heisenberg factor induction and scalar action on the other factors. At n=0 this is the one-dimensional trivial representation.

items.name: Common character and derived kernel
items.statement: Let k be a nonarchimedean local field of residue characteristic p, G a connected reductive k-group split by a tame extension, and p∤|W_abs(G)|. Set θ=∏_i φhat_i|K_+ and N^H=ker(θ|K_+^H). θ is the scalar K_+-character of the Yu tensor construction, independent of the depth-zero representation. Keep θ and N^H on their stated domains.

items.name: The given representation contains the common character
items.statement: Let k be a nonarchimedean local field of residue characteristic p, G a connected reductive k-group split by a tame extension, and p∤|W_abs(G)|. The compatible subspace Vtilde contains a one-dimensional K_+-subrepresentation with character θ; the Yu type representation restricts to a θ-isotypic representation.

items.name: Combined derived Heisenberg quotient
items.statement: Let k be a nonarchimedean local field of residue characteristic p, G a connected reductive k-group split by a tame extension, and p∤|W_abs(G)|. If n>0, K_0+^H/N^H is a finite Heisenberg p-group with center K_+^H/N^H of order p. The induced commutator form on K_0+^H/K_+^H is the orthogonal direct sum of the individual generic forms.

items.name: Zero-length derived quotient
items.statement: Let k be a nonarchimedean local field of residue characteristic p, G a connected reductive k-group split by a tame extension, and p∤|W_abs(G)|. If n=0, K_0+^H/N^H=K_+^H/N^H; with θ trivial this quotient is trivial. Do not apply a nontrivial-center uniqueness theorem to this branch.

items.name: Multiplicity-space factorization
items.statement: Let k be a nonarchimedean local field of residue characteristic p, G a connected reductive k-group split by a tame extension, and p∤|W_abs(G)|. For a compatible irreducible K-constituent Vhat containing the κ|K_0+ isotypic type, construct ρ=Hom_{K_0+}(κ,Vhat) with (g.f)(v)=π(g)f(κ(g)^{-1}v). Evaluation identifies ρ⊗κ≃Vhat; K_0+ acts trivially on ρ.

items.name: Irreducible depth-zero factor
items.statement: Let k be a nonarchimedean local field of residue characteristic p, G a connected reductive k-group split by a tame extension, and p∤|W_abs(G)|. The multiplicity representation ρ is irreducible as a K-representation, trivial on K_0+, and ρ⊗κ is isomorphic to the chosen Vhat.

items.name: Tensor factorization preserves datum invariants
items.statement: Let k be a nonarchimedean local field of residue characteristic p, G a connected reductive k-group split by a tame extension, and p∤|W_abs(G)|. The chosen Vhat is fixed by every (H_i)_x,r_i+ for 1≤i≤n+1.

items.name: Tensor factorization preserves all datum characters
items.statement: Let k be a nonarchimedean local field of residue characteristic p, G a connected reductive k-group split by a tame extension, and p∤|W_abs(G)|. For each i≤n the mixed quotient (H_i)_x,r_i,(r_i/2)+/(H_i)_x,r_i+ acts on Vhat by φ∘X_i.

items.name: Cuspidal representation of a finite reductive quotient
items.statement: For a connected reductive group over the finite residue field f, a complex irreducible representation is cuspidal if its invariants under the f-points of the unipotent radical of every proper f-parabolic vanish. This is the depth-zero quotient notion used for ρ, not a condition imposed initially on ρ_0.

items.name: Residual unipotent radical from a cocharacter
items.statement: For a reductive group over the finite field f and a proper f-parabolic, its unipotent radical is the subgroup contracted to the identity by a suitable f-defined cocharacter. Lift that cocharacter to the chosen parahoric torus before moving x.

items.name: Produce a larger-facet contained datum
items.statement: Let k be a nonarchimedean local field of residue characteristic p, G a connected reductive k-group split by a tame extension, and p∤|W_abs(G)|. If a constituent of ρ on the terminal reductive quotient has nonzero invariants under a proper unipotent radical U_f, decompose each V_i into positive/zero/negative weights for the lifted cocharacter. Combine U_f-fixed ρ-vectors with the corrected Weil invariant lines, and move x to x+ελ. The resulting nonzero subspace gives a contained datum with strictly larger terminal facet.

items.name: Depth-zero factor is cuspidal
items.statement: Let k be a nonarchimedean local field of residue characteristic p, G a connected reductive k-group split by a tame extension, and p∤|W_abs(G)|. For a maximal datum, every irreducible constituent of ρ|(G_{n+1})_x,0 is a cuspidal representation of (G_{n+1})_x,0/(G_{n+1})_x,0+. This is a theorem about ρ after removing κ, not about the naively character-untwisted Vtilde.

items.name: Kim–Yu input and reversed indexing
items.statement: Let k be a nonarchimedean local field of residue characteristic p, G a connected reductive k-group split by a tame extension, and p∤|W_abs(G)|. Reverse the chain and depths to Kim–Yu/Yu order, remove the duplicate G_1=G_2 when present, and append the terminal trivial character only in the other case. Take x, the depth-zero ρ on K_{G_{n+1}}, and the generic characters. Retain all D1–D5 conditions: the generic-embedding condition D2 is not automatic and is proved later; D5 is relative to the chosen point.

items.name: Half-depth generic-embedding defect
items.statement: Let k be a nonarchimedean local field of residue characteristic p, G a connected reductive k-group split by a tame extension, and p∤|W_abs(G)|. Set M_i=Cent_{G_i}(Z_s(M_{n+1})). For the commuting building-embedding diagram through these k-Levis, define D(x)=Σ_{i=1}^n(dim((G_i)_x,r_i/2/(G_i)_x,(r_i/2)+)−dim((M_i)_x,r_i/2/(M_i)_x,(r_i/2)+)). It is a nonnegative integer; the diagram is generic relative to the fixed ambient point x iff D(x)=0.

items.name: Perturb to a generic embedding diagram
items.statement: Let k be a nonarchimedean local field of residue characteristic p, G a connected reductive k-group split by a tame extension, and p∤|W_abs(G)|. If the defect is positive, KY17 Lemma3.6(b) gives a cocharacter of Z_s(M_{n+1}) and sufficiently small ε>0 making the diagram generic at x+ελ while the specified half-depth and full-depth groups shrink and the terminal depth-zero parahoric and radical remain unchanged.

items.name: Generic perturbation preserves maximal datum containment
items.statement: Let k be a nonarchimedean local field of residue characteristic p, G a connected reductive k-group split by a tame extension, and p∤|W_abs(G)|. Use isotropic Heisenberg fixed vectors after the perturbation to build a contained datum at x+ελ with the same terminal facet dimension, hence still maximal, and with defect zero.

items.name: A minimal-defect maximal datum has zero defect
items.statement: Let k be a nonarchimedean local field of residue characteristic p, G a connected reductive k-group split by a tame extension, and p∤|W_abs(G)|. Choose a maximal datum minimizing the nonnegative integer defect D. A positive value contradicts the previous perturbation, so the Kim–Yu generic-embedding condition holds.

items.name: Kim–Yu construction produces a covering type
items.statement: Let k be a nonarchimedean local field of residue characteristic p, G a connected reductive k-group split by a tame extension, and p∤|W_abs(G)|. For the full Kim–Yu input satisfying D1–D5, (K,ρ⊗κ) is an s-type and a cover of the corresponding type on M_1=Cent_G(Z_s(M_{n+1})). This is the KY17 construction/type/cover theorem, not a consequence of tensor irreducibility alone. Here the initial compact subgroup is the maximal compact stabilizer used in the main paper; with arbitrary smaller initial compact subgroup KY17 yields an S-type for a finite set S, not necessarily one s.

items.name: Every irreducible contains a Kim–Yu type
items.statement: Let k be a nonarchimedean local field of residue characteristic p, G a connected reductive k-group split by a tame extension, and p∤|W_abs(G)|. Every smooth irreducible complex representation of G(k) contains an s-type constructed by Kim and Yu.

items.name: Enhanced data determine the Bernstein component
items.statement: Let k be a nonarchimedean local field of residue characteristic p, G a connected reductive k-group split by a tame extension, and p∤|W_abs(G)|. For two Kim–Yu data with K_{M^0} and K_{Mdot^0} the maximal compact subgroups of their reduced-point fixers and satisfying the HM hypothesis C on their Levi chains, the resulting types are equivalent iff some g∈G(k) conjugates K_{M^0} to K_{Mdot^0} and identifies ρ_{M^0}⊗(∏φ_i)|M^0 with the corresponding twisted representation for the other datum. Kaletha's reduced-data equivalence removes C via z-extensions; close that adapter before declaring the unconditional enhancement criterion. Bare functional data do not determine the block.

items.name: Compact-mod-center inducing datum
items.statement: Let k be a nonarchimedean local field of residue characteristic p, G a connected reductive k-group split by a tame extension, and p∤|W_abs(G)|. For the supercuspidal branch replace (G_{n+1})_x by its reduced-building stabilizer (G_{n+1})_[x], extend the depth-zero factor compatibly, and form Ktilde=(G_{n+1})_[x](G_n)_x,r_n/2⋯(G_1)_x,r_1/2 with its tensor representation. Anisotropy of Z(G_{n+1})/Z(G) ensures compactness modulo Z(G)(k).

items.name: Supercuspidal support forces the cover Levi to be G
items.statement: Let k be a nonarchimedean local field of residue characteristic p, G a connected reductive k-group split by a tame extension, and p∤|W_abs(G)|. If a supercuspidal π contains the Kim–Yu covering type, then M_1=G. Consequently M_{n+1}=G_{n+1} and Z(G_{n+1})/Z(G) is anisotropic.

items.name: Depth-zero induction at the terminal reduced fixer
items.statement: Let k be a nonarchimedean local field of residue characteristic p, G a connected reductive k-group split by a tame extension, and p∤|W_abs(G)|. When M_{n+1}=G_{n+1}, x has minimal facet dimension and the terminal reduced-fixer representation has cuspidal parahoric restriction, its compact induction to G_{n+1}(k) is irreducible supercuspidal under the MP96 hypotheses used here.
items.locator: Theorem8.1 proof, [MP96] Proposition6.6; companion Remark2.3 refers to proof of Proposition6.8

items.name: Corrected Yu construction is irreducible supercuspidal
items.statement: For a tame connected reductive group over a nonarchimedean local field of odd residue characteristic, a Yu datum with strictly ordered positive depths, generic characters, terminal central quotient anisotropic, minimal terminal facet, and cuspidal terminal depth-zero representation yields irreducible supercuspidal c-Ind_{Ktilde}^{G(k)}(ρ⊗κ). Use Fintzen's corrected proof, avoiding the false Yu01 Proposition14.1/Theorem14.2.
items.locator: Theorem8.1 input; construction companion Theorem3.1 and §2.1

items.name: All supercuspidals arise from Yu's construction
items.statement: Let k be a nonarchimedean local field of residue characteristic p, G a connected reductive k-group split by a tame extension, and p∤|W_abs(G)|. Every smooth irreducible supercuspidal complex representation of G(k) is isomorphic to a representation obtained by Yu's construction. After obtaining the type, use the reduced-fixer inducing datum, corrected irreducibility and a nonzero Frobenius-reciprocity map.

items.name: Supercuspidal maximal-datum geometry is necessary
items.statement: Let k be a nonarchimedean local field of residue characteristic p, G a connected reductive k-group split by a tame extension, and p∤|W_abs(G)|. For any maximal datum (x,(X_i),ρ_0) in irreducible π, if π is supercuspidal, then the facet containing x has minimal dimension in B(G_{n+1},k) and Z(G_{n+1})/Z(G) is anisotropic, where G_{n+1}=Cent_G(ΣX_i).

items.name: Supercuspidal maximal-datum geometry is sufficient
items.statement: Let k be a nonarchimedean local field of residue characteristic p, G a connected reductive k-group split by a tame extension, and p∤|W_abs(G)|. For a maximal datum in irreducible π, minimal terminal facet dimension and anisotropy of Z(G_{n+1})/Z(G) imply π is supercuspidal. Maximality is essential to invoke the cuspidality of the extracted factor.

items.name: Separate the torus case
items.statement: Let k be a nonarchimedean local field of residue characteristic p, G a connected reductive k-group split by a tame extension, and p∤|W_abs(G)|. If G is a torus, its smooth irreducible complex representations are characters and are covered by the toral/depth-zero plus central-character construction. Do not deduce p odd from the trivial Weyl group or run the non-torus Heisenberg argument at p=2.
items.locator: §2 exclusion of tori; scope of Theorems7.12,8.1

items.name: Finite-group equivariant splitting
items.statement: For a field F, finite group H with |H| nonzero in F, and an injective F[H]-linear map f:V→W, there exists an F[H]-linear g:W→V with g∘f=id. In particular finite complex group representations are semisimple; this statement does not itself assert that a chosen smaller-group subspace lies in one larger-group constituent.

items.name: Compact smooth constituent and projection API
items.statement: For a compact totally disconnected group K and a smooth complex representation, each vector generates a finite-dimensional representation factoring through a finite quotient after passing to an open normal kernel. Use Maschke to obtain equivariant projections in that finite piece. Track the preservation of a specified compatible character space under the chosen projections.

items.name: Strict decrease of the next positive depth
items.statement: Let k be a nonarchimedean local field of residue characteristic p, G a connected reductive k-group split by a tame extension, and p∤|W_abs(G)|. At a positive recursion step j>1, r_j<r_{j−1}: the preceding functional X_{j−1} kills h_j, so the preceding contained datum makes (H_j)_x,r_{j−1} act trivially on its compatible space; a filtration gap lowers the admissible depth at that point, and global minimization preserves the strict upper bound. Also G_j≠Cent_{G_j}(X_j) for every j>1, since otherwise X_j kills h_j and the same gap contradicts minimality.

items.name: Generic-character intertwining reduction
items.statement: For the tame odd-residue-characteristic Yu setup and g∈G_i(k), if g intertwines φhat_i restricted to (G_i)_x,r_i,(r_i/2)+, then g∈(G_i)_x,r_i/2 G_{i+1}(k)(G_i)_x,r_i/2. Iterating restricts an intertwiner of the full inducing representation to Ktilde_n G_{n+1}(k) Ktilde_n.
items.locator: Construction companion Lemma3.4, first part of Theorem3.1; [Yu01] Theorem9.4

items.name: Terminal cuspidality forces the intertwiner into the fixer
items.statement: In the corrected Yu construction, a remaining intertwiner g∈G_{n+1}(k) not fixing [x] would yield a proper residual parabolic unipotent group fixing a nonzero vector in the cuspidal depth-zero factor. The Heisenberg isotropic invariants with their determinant twist separate the κ-action; hence g fixes [x] and lies in Ktilde.

items.name: The quadratic factor changes a finite invariant space
items.statement: For odd p and M=GL2(F_p) acting on functions on F_p² by a coordinate permutation times the quadratic determinant character, the invariant space is zero: every vector, including zero, has a stabilizer element of nonsquare determinant. Omitting the character gives two invariant orbit-functions. This finite calculation detects the sign that causes the Sp10 intertwining counterexample; it is not a disproof of Yu irreducibility.

items.name: Moy–Prasad depth of a representation
items.statement: Let k be a nonarchimedean local field of residue characteristic p, G a connected reductive k-group split by a tame extension, and p∤|W_abs(G)|. For smooth irreducible π, its pointwise depth at x is the least r≥0 with π^{G_x,r+}≠0, and its depth is the minimum over building points. Attainment and discreteness are Moy–Prasad theorems, not automatic properties of a real infimum.

items.name: Unrefined minimal K-type
items.statement: Let k be a nonarchimedean local field of residue characteristic p, G a connected reductive k-group split by a tame extension, and p∤|W_abs(G)|. The Moy–Prasad input is a depth-zero cuspidal irreducible representation of a finite reductive parahoric quotient, or at positive depth a character of the appropriate graded Moy–Prasad quotient represented by a nondegenerate dual coset. Keep this distinct from a Bernstein s-type and from the stronger functional datum of §4. In the positive-depth alternative, the dual coset X+g*_x,(-r)+ avoids the nilpotent cone under the chosen invariant-bilinear identification; the character is on G_x,r/G_x,r+.

items.name: Admissible complex representation
items.statement: Let k be a nonarchimedean local field of residue characteristic p, G a connected reductive k-group split by a tame extension, and p∤|W_abs(G)|. A smooth complex π is admissible if π^U is finite-dimensional for every compact open U. This finiteness is separate from smoothness and from the finite dimension of an individual compact-group constituent.

items.name: Irreducible complex representations are admissible
items.statement: Let k be a nonarchimedean local field of residue characteristic p, G a connected reductive k-group split by a tame extension, and p∤|W_abs(G)|. Every smooth irreducible complex representation of G(k) is admissible. This is imported from the basic local representation-theory owner, not deduced by assuming the tame-type classification.

items.name: Cover of a Levi type
items.statement: Let k be a nonarchimedean local field of residue characteristic p, G a connected reductive k-group split by a tame extension, and p∤|W_abs(G)|. Let M be a k-Levi, K compact open in G(k), K_M=K∩M(k), and irreducible ρ,ρ_M. The pair (K,ρ) covers (K_M,ρ_M) if for every opposite pair P=MU and Pbar=MUbar: K=(K∩U)K_M(K∩Ubar), ρ|K_M=ρ_M and both unipotent intersections act trivially, and the natural map V→V_U is injective on the (K,ρ)-isotypic subspace for every smooth V.
items.locator: Theorem8.1 input; KY17 §4.2, inspected v1 p4

items.name: Generic building embedding at a point and depth
items.statement: Let k be a nonarchimedean local field of residue characteristic p, G a connected reductive k-group split by a tame extension, and p∤|W_abs(G)|. For a k-Levi M⊂G, y∈B(M,k), real s and an embedding ι:B(M,k)→B(G,k), genericity at (y,s) means U_a,ι(y),s=U_a,ι(y),s+ for every relative root outside M. A chain diagram is generic if each component is generic at its specified depth.

items.name: Nongeneric embedding shifts form discrete root hyperplanes
items.statement: Let k be a nonarchimedean local field of residue characteristic p, G a connected reductive k-group split by a tame extension, and p∤|W_abs(G)|. For a tame Levi-chain diagram and prescribed depths, generic shifts exist. Along a vector pairing nontrivially with every outside root, nongeneric parameters form a discrete set; this gives arbitrarily small generic shifts. The root-coordinate containment refinements must still be checked.
items.locator: KY17 Lemma3.6(a),(b), inspected pp3–4; main Theorem7.12

items.name: Remove the HM equivalence hypothesis
items.statement: For tame connected reductive G over a nonarchimedean local field of odd residue characteristic, two reduced generic cuspidal G-data yield isomorphic Yu supercuspidal representations iff they are G-equivalent, without hypotheses C on their chains. Equivalence is generated by conjugation, isomorphism of the depth-zero representation and refactorization: the tail character ratios have depth at most the preceding depth and the depth-zero factor is twisted compatibly. Use z-extension descent as in Kal19 §3.5.
items.locator: Remark6.2 input; Kal19 Corollary3.5.5, selected proof and §2.1 inspected

routes.reason: The existing local-group owner already owns valued roots, enlarged buildings and connected parahorics. Add the real-depth Lie/dual, tame-descent, mixed-depth, torus-exactness and generic-embedding adapters there. Define these for general tame Levi pairs/chains independently of representation data, so the type-exhaustion theorem is a consumer, never an input to its own building foundation.

Reuse the smooth category, compact projections, Hecke corners, induction/Jacquet functors, complex admissibility and Bernstein theory. This adds the exact type-Hecke convention and local depth/character adapters without treating finite-group induction as p-adic compact induction or relying on later SR.6 integral finiteness.

The half-alternating-pairing central extension is one algebraic construction. Expose MP.0's generic characteristic-not-two carrier and its finite-field specialization, importing any existing abstract central extension API. The source-scoped generalization does not assert the characteristic-zero local Stone–von Neumann or metaplectic-cover theorem over finite fields. The finite representation theorems belong to the next continuation.

routes.title: Reductive algebraic groups, Part II: coadjoint stability and generic functionals
routes.reason: Upstream owns algebraic groups, roots, Lie algebras, dynamic parabolics and semisimple structure. The local RG2 continuation owns buildings and filtrations. Neither states the rational instability, lattice-compatible coadjoint centralizer and generic-approximation package used here. Existing arithmetic-torus, semiglobal, integral-representation and dominance candidates do not cover this target.
routes.brief: Begin after Reductive algebraic groups (tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/ReductiveGroups), the first prerequisite, importing its Lie, torus, derived-group, root and dynamic-parabolic APIs rather than rebuilding them. Import Reductive groups, Part II: local structure and arithmetic models (ReductiveGroupsPartII) for Moy–Prasad lattices and tame building descent, and Root systems (tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/RepresentationTheory/RootSystems) for finite root combinatorics. For a connected reductive group over a nonarchimedean local field, tame splitting and p not dividing the absolute Weyl order, prove Lemma2.2's separate prime consequences, invariant bilinear forms, closed coadjoint centralizers, and generic-functional depth/stability. Prove Proposition3.12 exactly: every nonzero almost strongly stable X at x admits an arbitrarily nearby x' and a generic representative congruent at x', with both points in its centralizer building. Construct rational residue-field destabilizing cocharacters, root projections and the depth-shifting bracket isomorphism first. Perfectness belongs to the residue field, not an assumed perfect local field. Include equal-characteristic examples and the exact-depth guard for central functionals. General roots and parabolics remain imports; the continuation owns only these additional stability/prime/lattice interfaces.

routes.title: Metaplectic groups, Weil representations and automorphic theta kernels, Part II: finite Heisenberg–Weil representations
routes.reason: The existing MP roadmap explicitly begins over characteristic-zero local fields. Finite odd-characteristic Weil modules and their corrected parabolic restriction require a separately sourced extension. The common Heisenberg carrier remains MP.0's single owner. The Mercurjev–Scavia finite Heisenberg special case should compare with this carrier, not create another generic construction.
routes.brief: Begin after Metaplectic groups, Weil representations and automorphic theta kernels (MetaplecticAutomorphicForms), the first prerequisite, importing MP.0's single algebraic Heisenberg carrier generalized to fields with 2 invertible. This is a finite-field representation branch, not an assertion that characteristic-zero analytic oscillator results specialize automatically. Import existing finite representation, group algebra, induction and Maschke APIs from Mathlib and tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/RepresentationTheory/InductionRestriction. For finite-dimensional symplectic F_p-spaces with p odd and a fixed nontrivial central character, construct Schrödinger modules, prove finite Stone–von Neumann uniqueness, construct the normalized Weil action of Sp(V), and prove the corrected Gérardin parabolic induction and isotropic-invariant formulas with the quadratic determinant character. Include zero symplectic dimension and prime 3. Test that the determinant-twisted GL2 permutation module on F_p² has no invariants whereas the untwisted module has two. Export these formulas to tame types; do not build global theta kernels, local character formulas or an unrelated new Heisenberg group. Compare the special finite Heisenberg group used in PAPER-MERKURJEV-SCAVIA-26 with the shared constructor.

routes.title: Smooth representations of local groups, Part II: tame types and supercuspidal exhaustion
routes.reason: SR.0–3 supplies the category and Bernstein foundations, not functional data, generic character extraction, Kim–Yu covers or the explicit tame-prime exhaustion theorem. Newton cocenters, parahoric centers, unitary spherical representations and all-rank GLn newforms have distinct endpoints. No LLC classification or later depth-zero Hecke-algebra equivalence is claimed.
routes.brief: Begin after Smooth representations of local groups (SmoothRepresentationsOfLocalGroups), the first prerequisite, importing SR.0–3 for the smooth complex category, type Hecke convention, compact induction, Jacquet functors, admissibility and Bernstein blocks. Import ReductiveGroupsPartII for buildings and filtrations, ReductiveGroupsPartIICoadjointStability for generic approximation, and MetaplecticPartIIFiniteWeil for the corrected finite Weil formulas; the last two are candidate suppliers, not yet accepted layers. For k of arbitrary characteristic, G connected reductive and tamely split, and residue p not dividing the absolute Weyl-group order, prove every smooth irreducible complex G(k)-representation contains a functional datum (Theorem6.1), then a Kim–Yu s-type (Theorem7.12), and every irreducible supercuspidal arises from Yu's construction (Theorem8.1). Prove both directions of Corollary8.3 for a maximal datum: supercuspidality is equivalent to minimal terminal-facet dimension and anisotropic terminal center modulo Z(G). Build the depth-minimizing recursion, character extensions, tensor multiplicity factor, genuine depth-zero cuspidality and zero embedding-defect argument. Keep bare data, types and compact-mod-center inducing data distinct. Use Fintzen's corrected Yu irreducibility proof, not Yu14.1/14.2, and close all source gaps before acceptance. Handle n=0, G_1=G_2, tori and the finite Weil quadratic sign explicitly; this is not a modular-coefficient or residue-two generalization.
